title: Chopin, Waltz Op. 64 No. 1, in three recordings
work: Waltz in D♭ major, Op. 64 No. 1
question: How much time does each pianist take over the middle section before the circling figure returns?
intro: Chopin opens the Minute Waltz with the right hand playing a short figure of notes that circles back on itself. A slower middle section, marked sostenuto, comes between the fast passages. Rachmaninoff, Olga Gurevich and Muriel Nguyen Xuan each play this middle section before the trill leads back into the opening figure.

recordings.label: Sergei Rachmaninoff, 1923
recordings.note: Rachmaninoff recorded Chopin’s dance for Victor on 5 April 1923, playing a Steinway concert grand.

recordings.label: Olga Gurevich, c. 2014
recordings.note: Born in Baku, Gurevich moved to Moscow at seventeen to study piano at the Gnesin Academy.

recordings.label: Muriel Nguyen Xuan, 2007
recordings.note: Nguyen Xuan plays a Yamaha grand. Stéphane Magnenat recorded her on 16 July 2007.

passages.label: Opening figure around A♭
passages.note: The right hand turns around A♭, then moves into a running melody. Bass notes and two answering chords keep up the waltz accompaniment.

passages.label: Sostenuto middle section
passages.note: The quick notes stretch into a sustained melody, marked sostenuto. The left hand keeps its three-beat dance underneath.

passages.label: Return of the opening figure
passages.note: The circling figure returns after the long trill, and the bass rejoins it. The running melody starts again.
